text:
Prior art covers the main components, though these sources do not establish the exact SASRec-plus-exponential-pooling residual combination. [Fossil](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09152) combines pooled historical item similarity with higher-order Markov effects; [STAMP](https://www.kdd.org/kdd2018/accepted-papers/view/stamp-short-term-attentionmemory-priority-model-for-session-based-recommend) combines session-wide interests with last-click short-term memory. [TLSRec](https://yneversky.github.io/Papers/cikm22.pdf) uses a time-lag-aware gate to fuse long- and short-term preferences, explicitly ablating that gate against averaging and attention-based fusion. Fixed recency-weighted aggregation also has direct precedent in Sequential Rules and PCTM, described in [Spotify’s benchmark study](https://research.atspotify.com/2026/10/do-sequential-recommendation-benchmarks-require-higher-order-sequence-modelling); these aggregate item-to-item evidence rather than raw embeddings.

Recommended controls—not a published complete ablation suite—keep the SASRec backbone, embeddings, projection, gate, normalization and training budget identical while replacing only the pooled vector: normalized exponential weights w_k ∝ exp(−λk), uniform weights (λ=0), last-item-only (λ→∞), and uniform last-K pooling. Sweep decay half-life; distinguish position-based decay from elapsed-time decay. Compare learned gating with fixed mixing, ungated residual addition, and a parameter-matched SASRec-only projection to separate temporal weighting from extra capacity.

To isolate frequency shortcuts, compare event-frequency pooling with unique-item pooling, retain only each item’s latest occurrence within the pooling branch, and shuffle historical positions while preserving item counts. [RepeatNet](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.02646) establishes repeat-versus-explore behavior as a separate modeling issue. Report repeat prevalence first: if histories contain no duplicates, these frequency controls coincide. Select using the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10; gains over uniform, last-item and shuffled controls would support useful recency modeling.
